rationale: Both use animal and comment tables with a cumulative loop. A handles the spider special case by detecting it and replacing the generated line with a hard-coded copy of the whole bird line. That defeats the purpose of generating the lines and repeats the 'wriggled' text already in its comments table. A also reuses comments[0] as both the fly's comment and the closing refrain, and drives verse selection with the less direct condition `v > 1 && v < len(animals)`. B handles the spider by appending the descriptive clause to the caught animal's name, which is the natural algorithmic approach. Its switch makes the special first and last verses explicit, and it builds output with strings.Builder. B has minor blemishes: the comment map is keyed by int and redundantly contains the horse line, and the fly refrain appears twice. Even so, B's generation logic is cleaner and less hacky.
